claim: Failure to pay tax shown on the return: 0.5% of unpaid tax per month or fraction of a month, capped at 10% in total.
establishes: A.R.S. 42-1125(D) late-payment penalty rate, accrual and cap.
uncertainty: No minimum penalty found in the statute or on ADOR's penalty page.
designImplication: Model AZ late payment as 0.5%/month (partial month counts as a month) up to 10%; no floor.

claim: Failure to file: 4.5% of the tax required to be shown per month or fraction of a month, max 25%. The failure-to-file (A) and failure-to-pay (D) penalties combined may not exceed 25%.
establishes: A.R.S. 42-1125(A) rate and the combined A+D 25% cap; confirmed in plain language at https://azdor.gov/individuals/income-tax-filing-assistance/filing-notices-penalties-and-interest.
uncertainty: Minimum: NOT FOUND (none stated).
designImplication: Late filing + late payment together cap at 25% of tax.

claim: An additional 25% of the tax applies when a taxpayer fails to file after the department's notice and demand; it stacks on top of the 42-1125(A) failure-to-file penalty.

value.trigger: failure to file after notice and demand

establishes: A.R.S. 42-1125(B) non-filer demand penalty.
uncertainty: Days allowed to respond to the demand are set by A.R.S. 42-1109 (15 days, below), not by 42-1125.
designImplication: A non-filer who ignores a demand can reach 25% (A+D) + 25% (B) = 50% of tax in penalties.

claim: Interest = federal short-term rate + 3 points (IRC 6621 method), same for under- and overpayments; compounded annually: each Jan 1 ADOR adds outstanding interest to the principal. Rates: 2025 7%; 2026 Q1 7%, Q2 6%, Jul 1-Dec 31 2026 7% (daily 0.0001918).
establishes: Late-2026 AZ interest rate, the daily rate and annual compounding. Statutory basis is A.R.S. 42-1123 (https://www.azleg.gov/ars/42/01123.htm), which says 'compounded annually'.
uncertainty: Whether interest accrues on penalties: NOT FOUND (42-1123 is silent).
designImplication: Daily simple accrual within a year at 7%, with the balance capitalised every Jan 1.

claim: Individuals request a monthly installment plan on AZTaxes.gov. Setup takes up to 2 weeks if a bill has been issued, up to 8 weeks if not. No new liabilities may be incurred while on a plan; interest keeps accruing. If the plan defaults, ADOR 'can and will enforce without notice through a levy and/or lien action'.

value.apply: AZTaxes.gov > Individual > Request a Payment Plan

establishes: AZ plan application, processing time, the new-liability rule and default handling.
uncertainty: No max balance, max term or fee is published. The page https://azdor.gov/individuals/payment-arrangement-individuals adds that delinquent returns must be filed within 30 days and a financial statement may be required.
designImplication: AZ plan: no cure period on default, and any new balance breaks the plan.

claim: ADOR may alter, modify or terminate an installment agreement if the taxpayer misses an installment or any other liability, fails to file a return when due, fails to furnish requested info within 30 days, or collection is in jeopardy. Any refund is applied first to delinquent tax 'whether or not you have a current installment arrangement', and the offset does not replace the scheduled installment. A lien may be filed alongside a plan.
establishes: AZ plan default triggers and refund offset during a plan.
uncertainty: Publication dated 2014. Still hosted by ADOR.
designImplication: A refund offset during an AZ plan reduces the balance but still leaves the next monthly payment due.

claim: A tax billing notice (demand for payment) begins collection; at least one bill is mailed. Documents marked 'Final Demand' / 'Final Notice' follow. Enforcement: Notice of Levy, Notice of Tax Lien, seizure and sale, lawsuit. A bank levy holds funds up to the amount owed for 21 days, then the bank remits. A wage levy is continuous until the balance is paid. A sale needs at least 10 days' notice.

value.wageLevy: continuous; portion based on allowance per dependent

establishes: AZ collection steps and bank-levy hold period.
uncertainty: Days between the bill and the final notice, and between the final notice and a levy: NOT FOUND. Notice form numbers: NOT FOUND. Collection fee: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: For AZ, model a bill, then a final demand, then a levy, with the gaps unparameterised (a game-design choice) and a 21-day bank-levy hold.

claim: If a taxpayer fails to file within 15 days after written demand, the department may estimate taxable income from any available information and propose to assess tax, interest and penalties. Hearings need at least 10 days' written notice.

value.penalties: 42-1125(A) 4.5%/mo to 25% + 42-1125(B) 25% failure to file on demand

establishes: A.R.S. 42-1109 estimated assessment for non-filers.
uncertainty: How long after the due date ADOR typically sends the demand: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: AZ non-filer: a demand, then 15 days, then an estimated proposed assessment.

claim: NOT FOUND: no published order for applying a partial payment to tax, penalty or interest.
establishes: Absence of a published rule on ADOR's collections pages.
uncertainty: May exist in the administrative code; not located.
designImplication: Pick a default and label it a design assumption.

claim: State refunds are applied to ADOR debt first, then to other state liabilities (child support, courts, agencies, municipalities; the page also lists the IRS). ADOR participates in the federal Treasury Offset Program. A claim stays with the IRS until paid and carries across years. 30-day appeal window from the offset letter.
establishes: AZ state refund offset priority and TOP participation.
uncertainty: Multistate/reciprocal offset with other states: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: An AZ resident's federal refund can be taken for an AZ balance (subject to the federal TOP rules in the US entry).

claim: A single delinquent payment penalty for late filing or late payment: the greater of $5 or 5% of unpaid tax plus 0.5% for each full or partial month unpaid, max 12% total. Waived if 90% was paid by the original due date, the return was filed by the extended date, and the rest was paid with it.
sourceDate: Tax Topics: Penalties and Interest, July 2026
establishes: CO combines late filing and late payment into one delinquency penalty with a $5 floor and a 12% cap.
uncertainty: The waiver conditions come from the Individual Income Tax Guide (https://tax.colorado.gov/individual-income-tax-guide, Jan 2026).
designImplication: CO has no separate filing penalty: a late return with no tax due owes no delinquency penalty.

claim: If a taxpayer receives a notice of final determination and demand for payment and neither pays nor sets up a payment plan, the law requires a collection penalty of 15% of the unpaid tax.

value.trigger: final determination and demand not paid and no plan

establishes: CO 15% collection penalty.
uncertainty: How many days after the demand the penalty is added: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: A one-time 15% step at the final demand, separate from the 12% delinquency cap.

claim: 2026 rates: discounted 8%, regular 11% (2025: 9% / 12%). The discounted rate applies if paid before the notice of deficiency, within 30 days of it, or if an installment agreement is entered within 30 days. Accrues from the original due date; the daily rate is the annual rate / 365 (366 in a leap year).

value.onPenalties: no (per the Income Tax Guide summary)

establishes: CO late-2026 interest rates and the discounted/regular split.
uncertainty: The simple-not-compound and not-on-penalties statements came through a page summariser and were not confirmed verbatim. The rate table is also in the Individual Income Tax Guide (Jan 2026).
designImplication: Two-rate interest: paying or entering a plan within 30 days of the notice cuts the rate by 3 points.

claim: Standard plans run up to 36 months for non-business accounts; extended plans are available on hardship by phone. No additional fee, but late-payment penalties and interest continue. Apply via Revenue Online or by phone (303-205-8291); for current-year individual debt, a phone request must wait until after April 15. Plan violations: missed or short monthly payment, signed agreement not returned within 30 days, future returns not filed, NSF payment. On violation 'the entire balance of tax, penalty, and interest will become due immediately'. Future state refunds are applied to the debt even on a plan.
establishes: CO plan term, fee and default.
uncertainty: The max balance for an online plan is not published.
designImplication: CO: 36 months, free; default accelerates the whole balance.

topic: installment plan default and new balances
claim: The FAQ says CDOR notifies the taxpayer in writing if the plan is violated and that the taxpayer may call Collections before cancellation. Plan terms require new tax bills to be paid when due; failing that may cancel the plan, though new debt can potentially be rolled into the existing plan by contacting Collections. Refunds reduce the debt, but monthly payments must continue.

value.newBalance: must be paid when due; may be added by contacting Collections; otherwise may cancel

establishes: CO plan handling of new balances and default notice.
uncertainty: No numeric cure period.
designImplication: CO lets a new balance join the plan on request; AZ and HI do not.

claim: Notice of Deficiency (30 days to dispute), then Notice of Final Determination and Demand for Payment, then Notice of Intent to Issue Judgment/Lien (10 days to pay in full), then lien, collection agency, wage/bank levy and refund offsets. Before a levy CDOR 'usually' sends a Notice of Intent to Issue Tax Levy. A wage levy is generally 25% of disposable pay; a bank levy is a one-time sweep up to the full balance. Collection agencies may add a fee of up to 20% of the total tax, penalties and fees collected, which CDOR cannot waive.

notices: Notice of Final Determination and Demand for Payment
Notice of Intent to Issue Judgment/Lien (10 days)
Notice of Intent to Issue Tax Levy

establishes: CO collection steps and day counts.
uncertainty: Wage and bank levy details are from https://tax.colorado.gov/wage-garnishments; the agency fee is from the glossary. Days between the final determination and the lien notice: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: CO escalation stacks a 15% collection penalty and an agency fee of up to 20%.

claim: If an individual fails or refuses to file, the executive director may file a return on the individual's behalf with the information available; the assessment from it is 'as good and sufficient as' one based on a taxpayer-filed return.

value.method: department files a return on available information
value.penalty: delinquent payment penalty (5% + 0.5%/mo, max 12%) per general rule

establishes: CO substitute-return authority.
uncertainty: Timing after the due date and the demand-notice name: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: CO non-filers get a department-prepared return, then the normal deficiency path.

claim: Only partially published: 'If a required payment is not remitted or is underpaid, the Department will first credit any subsequent payments toward the amount due, regardless of when the payment is received.' The split between tax, penalty and interest was NOT FOUND.
establishes: Payments go to the oldest underpaid amount first (estimated-tax context).
uncertainty: The statement sits in the estimated-payment section.
designImplication: Do not claim a CO tax/penalty/interest order.

claim: Overpayments are applied to state tax liabilities and to other Colorado debts (unemployment repayment, child support, public assistance, state student loans, judicial fines). CDOR applies 'state or federal income tax refunds' to tax debt, i.e. it uses the federal offset. A CO refund may also go to federal tax debt through the IRS State Income Tax Levy Program.
establishes: CO offsets its own refunds and uses federal refund offset.
uncertainty: The list of offset debts and SITLP come from the Individual Income Tax Guide (Jan 2026). Multistate: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: CO refunds flow both ways: federal to the CO debt, and CO to the federal debt.

claim: 5% of the tax not paid by the original due date, plus 5% for each additional month the return is late, max 25%. O.C.G.A. 48-7-57.
establishes: GA failure-to-file rate and cap.
uncertainty: Whether a partial month counts is not stated verbatim on the page.
designImplication: Mirrors the federal 5%/month structure.

claim: 0.5% of the unpaid tax plus 0.5% of the outstanding tax for each additional month, max 25%. The late-filing and late-payment penalties combined cannot exceed 25% of the tax due on the return due date. O.C.G.A. 48-7-86.
establishes: GA late-payment rate, cap and combined cap.
uncertainty: none material
designImplication: Combined cap of 25%.

claim: Interest = Federal Reserve bank prime rate + 3%, set each January. For calendar year 2026 the annual rate is 9.75%, accruing monthly.
establishes: GA late-2026 interest rate.
uncertainty: Whether interest accrues on penalties: NOT FOUND. Compounding: NOT FOUND (stated only as 'accruing monthly').
designImplication: Use 9.75%/12 per month for 2026.

claim: Requirements: not in bankruptcy, no pending OIC, last five years of returns filed. Term up to 60 months; minimum payment $25/month. Apply on the Georgia Tax Center (More > Payments and Returns > Request Payment Plan) or by Form GA-9465. DOR usually decides within 30 days. Fees: the web page says $50 for auto-draft (added to the balance) or $100 for paper-check plans; Form GA-9465 (Rev. 07/15/25) says $50, reduced to $25 if income is under $22,050, plus $50 for a modification. Payments are applied 'in the best interests of the State of Georgia'.
establishes: GA plan term, minimum and fees.
uncertainty: The two official sources disagree on fees ($100 paper-check fee vs a $25 low-income reduction). Form: https://dor.georgia.gov/document/form/installmentpaymentagreementrequestinstructionsga946592816-1pdf/download
designImplication: GA plan: 60 months, $50 fee.

topic: installment plan default, new balances, refunds
claim: Default if payments are late or any balance due on a later return is unpaid. DOR may then file a state tax execution or levy/garnish to collect the entire amount. A tax execution adds a 20% collection fee. DOR sends a Payment Plan Default letter with a due date: pay by it or the plan is cancelled. Any future refund, state or federal, is applied to the plan liability; regular payments continue. The signer waives further notice and appeal rights on the plan liability.

value.curePeriod: due date stated in the default letter (days NOT FOUND)
value.newBalance: defaults the plan; a new plan carries new fees

establishes: GA plan default and refund handling.
uncertainty: The default letter page is https://dor.georgia.gov/payment-plan-default-letter; it has no day count.
designImplication: GA allows a one-letter cure; a new unpaid balance defaults the plan.

claim: Notice of Proposed Assessment (45 days to protest), then Official Assessment and Demand for Payment (45 days to appeal to the Tax Court or superior court). If neither paid nor appealed within 45 days, DOR may issue a State Tax Execution (a lien, recordable in county records) and impose a 20% collection fee. After that DOR may use garnishment, bank levy, property levy and sale. Other letters: Statement of Taxpayer's Account, Notice to Taxpayer of Right against Levy.

notices.name: Official Assessment and Demand for Payment
Notice to Taxpayer of Right against Levy

establishes: GA notice ladder and the 20% collection fee.
uncertainty: Letter list from https://dor.georgia.gov/did-you-get-letter. Days between the execution and a levy: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: About 90 days from the proposed assessment to an execution, at which point a 20% fee lands.

claim: DOR sends a Notice to Submit Return when an expected return was not received, with a deadline in the letter. If there is no response, DOR may estimate the tax due from the best information available, issue an assessment for it, and pursue collection.

value.responseDays: NOT FOUND (deadline stated on the letter)

establishes: GA non-filer process.
uncertainty: Timing after the due date: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: GA non-filer: a notice, then an estimated assessment, then the normal 45/45 ladder.

claim: 'All payments received will be applied to your account in the best interests of the State of Georgia.' No fixed tax/penalty/interest order published.
establishes: GA reserves discretion over payment application.
uncertainty: Fixed order NOT FOUND.
designImplication: Treat as discretionary.

claim: DOR does not issue refunds to those with outstanding state tax debt; refunds are offset until the debt is paid. GA participates in the Treasury Offset Program: it sends an Intent to Offset Notice by certified mail before requesting the federal refund. Under the setoff debt collection article, refunds of $25 or more are set off for claimant agencies (DHS, Georgia Student Finance Authority and others).

value.preOffsetNotice: Intent to Offset Notice, certified mail

establishes: GA TOP participation and state offset.
uncertainty: State offset statement: https://dor.georgia.gov/payment-plans-faq. Claimant-agency setoff (O.C.G.A. 48-7-160 to -170) is from a secondary source (Justia, https://law.justia.com/codes/georgia/title-48/chapter-7/article-7/section-48-7-164/), not verified verbatim. Multistate: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: A GA debt can take a GA resident's federal refund after a certified notice.

claim: Failure to file: 5% of the tax required to be shown for not more than one month, plus 5% for each additional month or fraction, max 25% in aggregate. The tax base is reduced by timely payments and credits.
sourceDate: HRS ch. 231 unofficial compilation as of 2025-12-31
uncertainty: none material
designImplication: Same structure as federal and GA.

claim: If a return is filed on time but the tax shown is not paid within 60 days of the prescribed filing date: up to 20% of the unpaid tax 'as determined by the director' (one-time, not monthly). This penalty applies only to timely-filed returns; a late return gets the 5%/month failure-to-file penalty instead.
establishes: HRS 231-39(b)(3); the N-11 instructions (Rev. Dec 2025) state it as a flat 20%.
uncertainty: The statute says 'up to' 20%; the instructions say 20%.
designImplication: HI is a cliff, not a meter: 0 until day 60, then 20%. Late filing and late payment don't stack.

claim: Two-thirds of 1% per month or fraction of a month (8%/year), from the first calendar day after the payment due date. No interest on interest. Instructions: interest is assessed 'on unpaid taxes and penalties'. The rate is fixed by statute, not indexed.
establishes: HI interest rate, accrual and that it runs on penalties.
uncertainty: Statute HRS 231-39(b)(4) in https://files.hawaii.gov/tax/legal/hrs/hrs_231.pdf. Penalties 'become part of the tax' under 231-39(b), which is why interest runs on them.
designImplication: Fixed 8%: unlike AZ/GA/IL, the rate doesn't move with the federal rate.

claim: Available if the unpaid balance is over $100, no active plan, not in bankruptcy, not referred to a private collection agency, no pending OIC. Non-refundable $50 processing fee (HRS 231-25.5). Apply on Hawaii Tax Online or by Form D-100. A plan over 12 months requires Form CM-2 financial statement, and a state tax lien will be initiated for plans over a year. Interest and penalties continue. Any state or federal refund is applied to the balance, and the monthly payment is still due. Any new liability puts the existing plan in default; a new plan must be requested. The taxpayer must contact the collector at least 7 business days before a payment they cannot make.
establishes: HI plan terms.
uncertainty: Web page https://tax.hawaii.gov/collections/payment-plans/ (2025-07-18) agrees. Max term not published.
designImplication: HI: $50 fee; a new balance defaults the plan; plans over a year carry a lien.

claim: Failure to comply is default, after which DOTAX may file a lien, levy, garnish, or refer to the Attorney General or a private collection agency for the entire amount. The Taxpayer Bill of Rights says taxpayers will be notified before collection action if the agreement is not in good standing.
sourceDate: N-11 instructions, Taxpayer Bill of Rights section IX (Rev. Dec 2025)
establishes: HI default consequence and pre-action notice.
uncertainty: Cure period length NOT FOUND.
designImplication: A notice comes before enforcement after a default, but no stated cure window.

claim: Cost recovery fees may be charged only after DOTAX mails a written demand warning of collection action. The demand must give a deadline of at least 10 calendar days after mailing. $50 for processing a delinquent account is charged at the close of that deadline if any part is unpaid; $15 per garnishment/levy service plus costs; $25 per lien recording; reasonable collection-agency or attorney fees actually incurred. No interest accrues on fees. A wage levy takes 25% of gross wages, continuously.
establishes: HI demand-notice minimum period and fee schedule.
uncertainty: Wage levy rate from https://tax.hawaii.gov/collections/wage-levy-for-individuals/ and HRS 231-25. Notice names and the gaps between routine billing notices: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: HI: a demand, then at least 10 days, then a $50 fee and enforcement; $15 per levy.

claim: If a taxpayer fails, neglects or refuses to file, the department shall make a return from the best information obtainable and assess the tax plus the 231-39 penalties and interest. The assessment is presumed correct; the burden is on the taxpayer. No limitations period for assessment when no return is filed.

value.method: department makes return from best information

uncertainty: The no-time-limit statement is from the N-11 Taxpayer Bill of Rights. Proposed assessment: 30 days to object (N-11 TBOR section V).
designImplication: HI non-filer: the department makes a return, then a proposed assessment with 30 days to object.

claim: For a partial payment of a delinquent amount, the amount is credited first to cost recovery fees, in the order charged. The order among tax, penalty and interest after fees was NOT FOUND.
establishes: HI fees-first rule.
uncertainty: Remaining order not published.
designImplication: Apply HI partial payments to fees first.

claim: State refunds are set off against debts certified by claimant agencies (HRS 231-53), and credits from other taxes may offset liabilities. Federal refund offset ('IRS Refund Offset program'): conditions were an individual income tax liability over $100, a lien filed, the taxpayer notified and allowed 60 days, and no bankruptcy.
establishes: HI participation in federal refund offset.
uncertainty: The TOP conditions come from a 2002 DOTAX newsletter and may be stale. The plan form (Rev. 2025) confirms federal refunds are applied. HRS 231-26 recognises other states' tax claims by comity in court, but that is not a refund-offset program. Multistate offset: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: A HI federal offset requires a filed lien; treat the threshold as dated.

claim: Returns due on or after 2024-01-01: 2% of any amount paid no later than 30 days after the due date; 10% if paid later than 30 days but before an audit/investigation starts; 20% if paid after an audit starts, reduced to 15% if the entire amount is paid within 30 days after the audit-prepared return or waiver. One-time tiered rates, not monthly.
establishes: IL late-payment penalty structure.
uncertainty: Pub-103 (Sept 2025) phrases the audit tiers slightly differently; the statute is used here.
designImplication: A step function: 2%, then 10% after day 30.

claim: Tier 1: 2% of the tax required to be shown (reduced by timely payments and credits), max $250. Tier 2: if the return isn't filed within 30 days after a notice of nonfiling, an additional greater of $250 or 2% of tax shown (without regard to timely payments), max $5,000, assessed even if no tax is due. When both apply, the late-filing and late-payment penalties are summed.
establishes: IL late-filing penalty tiers and how they combine.
uncertainty: Statute 35 ILCS 735/3-3(a-10) agrees.
designImplication: IL's filing penalty is small and capped in dollars; a nonfiling notice gives a $250 floor.

claim: Rate = IRC 6621 underpayment rate, reset Jan 1 and Jul 1. 7% for 01/01/2025 to 12/31/2026. Simple interest on a daily basis (tax x rate / 365 x days). For returns due after 2000 it accrues on tax only, not penalty. If tax is paid within 30 days of notice and demand, no interest accrues after the notice date.
establishes: IL late-2026 rate and computation.
uncertainty: Computation and the penalty exclusion are from 35 ILCS 735/3-2(c-5) (https://www.ilga.gov/Documents/legislation/ilcs/documents/003507350K3-2.htm).
designImplication: IL: interest on tax only; paying within 30 days of the bill freezes it.

claim: Plans are for hardship. Payment amount and length are based on financial condition. All returns must be filed. Apply on MyTax Illinois (the balance must already be actively in collection, not just a final notice) or by Form CPP-1 with a good-faith down payment. Over $15,000 requires Form EG-13-I. 'All outstanding liabilities will be part of the same payment plan.' No IDOR fee (card convenience fees aside). Default (missed payment, unfiled returns, taxes not paid when due) lets IDOR cancel the plan; the entire unpaid balance becomes due, and IDOR may levy bank accounts or wages. IDOR may file a lien at any time.
establishes: IL plan terms.
uncertainty: Also https://tax.illinois.gov/forms/misc/paymentplan.html. Refund offset during a plan is not stated on the plan pages, but 35 ILCS 5/909 lets IDOR credit any overpayment against liability.
designImplication: IL folds new balances into the plan instead of defaulting it.

claim: Notice of Tax Due (IDOR-2-BILL), then Notice of Deficiency (LTR-393-IPD), then referral to collections. If a bill for final liability isn't paid in full within 30 days, a cost of collection fee is added: $30 if under $1,000 unpaid, $100 if $1,000 or more. Enforcement: lien, seizure, wage levy (up to 15% of gross, with at least 10 days' notice before it goes to the employer), bank levy (bank holds funds for 20 days, then remits), license holds, and private collection agencies, whose fees the taxpayer pays.

costOfCollectionFee.trigger: 30 days after bill for final liability

establishes: IL collection steps and fees.
uncertainty: The fee is from Pub-103 (Sept 2025), the notice names from https://tax.illinois.gov/individuals/letters.html. Days between notices: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: A flat $30/$100 fee at 30 days; levies at 15% of wages.

claim: If the taxpayer fails to file, IDOR determines the tax due 'according to its best judgment and information' (prima facie correct) and issues a notice of deficiency. It becomes an assessment 60 days after issue (150 if outside the US) unless protested. Tier-2 nonfiling penalty if not filed within 30 days of a notice of nonfiling. No limitations period when no return is filed (35 ILCS 5/905(c)).
establishes: IL non-filer assessment process.
uncertainty: 905(c) came via secondary search results, not fetched.
designImplication: IL non-filer: a nonfiling notice, then 30 days, then a deficiency notice, then 60 days to assessment.

claim: NOT FOUND: no published order for applying a partial payment to tax, penalty and interest.
establishes: Absence on the IDOR collection page.
uncertainty: May be in 86 Ill. Adm. Code; not located.
designImplication: Label any order as an assumption.

claim: IDOR may credit an overpayment against any income tax liability (35 ILCS 5/909). Refund withholding priority: (1) unpaid State tax, (2) child support, (3) other State debts, (4) IRS tax, (4.5) federal nontax debt, (4.6) local government debts, (5) other states' tax claims under 911.2, (6) circuit clerk fees. The IDOR collection page says the IRS may redirect federal refunds to the IL debt (TOP). Reciprocal offset with other states: 35 ILCS 5/911.2 lets a 'claimant state' that extends like comity certify a final income tax debt and have IL withhold the refund (30 days to protest).

value.multistateReciprocal: authorised by statute for comity states; participating states NOT FOUND

establishes: IL refund withholding priority and the reciprocal multistate authority.
uncertainty: 911.2 text: https://www.ilga.gov/Documents/legislation/ilcs/documents/003500050K911.2.htm. Which states have agreements: NOT FOUND.
designImplication: IL is the only state of the five with a published reciprocal multistate offset statute.

topic: federal TOP rules (applies to all five states)
claim: Federal refund offset for a state income tax obligation requires the State to notify the debtor by certified mail, return receipt requested, give at least 60 days to dispute, and the address on the federal return must be within the State seeking the offset. Order: child support, then federal agency debts, then state debts.
sourceDate: 31 CFR 285.8 as reproduced by Cornell LII (secondary host of official text); accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: Federal preconditions for any of these states to take a federal refund.
uncertainty: Cornell LII is a secondary host; eCFR redirected and could not be fetched. 26 USC 6402(e) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6402) carries the same conditions. The 2010 Claims Resolution Act dropped residency for unemployment-compensation debts, not state income tax.
designImplication: A taxpayer who moves out of state shields a federal refund from the old state's income-tax TOP offset.
